primary_meaning: Heavenly glory, the firmament, or the throne of God (divine presence and celestial realm)

alternatives.meaning: One of the foundation stones of the New Jerusalem (eschatological glory or apostolic foundation)
Gem on the high priest’s breastplate (tribal or priestly representation)
Purity, truth, or heavenly-mindedness (linked to blue color and contemplative virtue in later Christian gem symbolism)
Specific apostolic or virtue associations in some medieval lists (e.g., linked to particular apostles or theological virtues)

notes: The throne/heaven association drawn from the theophany and chariot-throne texts is the most consistently cited symbolic reading in Christian biblical interpretation; other uses are largely catalog or decorative rather than primary symbols.
